title: Work: Mayfair Lumber and Gärtnerabo | MonoBook
description: Two identities. Mayfair Lumber Sales Ltd, a mark refined after four decades. Gärtnerabo, a garden care brand built new.
_h1Source: case study PDF page 20, 'Two ways to rebrand'

blocks.lead: Know the mark? Fix what is broken. New to the market? Start from zero.

rows.label: Who
rows.text: A wholesale lumber company in Alberta, Canada, more than four decades old.

rows.label: What we did
rows.text: We rebuilt their mark, colour and type.

rows.label: How it was run
rows.text: By email and video call, from Satkhira to Alberta.

blocks.heading: Small things showed at every size.
blocks._source: case study PDF page 5 ('in 1976' left out for the number rule)
paras: The original mark was made by hand. After more than four decades, corners did not match, the space on both sides was uneven, and the lines of text sat on mixed alignments.
None of it was loud. All of it made the brand look less certain than the company is.

blocks.heading: Fix only what is broken.
paras: Changing a mark people already know is a risk. So the brief was narrow: fix only what is broken, and keep everything people recognise.

blocks.heading: Four colours. Use them as written.
Two typefaces, each with one job.
blocks._source: case study PDF page 13 (heading written to summarise the page)

blocks.heading: Send your brief.
blocks.text: You hear back within two hours, UK working hours.
